_comment: Lighthouse CI (audit item B20, 2026-08-16). Thresholds below are DERIVED from measured runs, not chosen — see _baseline. Every value is an `error`, and the job no longer carries continue-on-error: a threshold that cannot fail is a comment.
_baseline: Two rounds of 3 runs on ubuntu-latest, desktop preset. Before the LCP preload (a8f1c95): perf 97-99 · a11y 95 · best-practices 100 · SEO 100 · LCP 719-731ms · TBT 83-142ms · CLS 0 · SI 660-791ms. After it (6e14f24): perf 96-98 · a11y 95 · LCP 581-613ms · TBT 109-163ms · SI 729-773ms. The prioritize-lcp-image audit went 0.5 to 1, which the preload definitely caused; LCP also measured ~130ms lower with non-overlapping ranges, more than the 20ms Lighthouse itself estimated — 3 runs a side on shared CI runners makes that suggestive, not proven.
_how_these_numbers_were_picked: Each threshold sits well BELOW the measured worst, deliberately, the same way the coverage floor in vite.config.ts does. Be honest about what that buys: these catch a REGRESSION (perf falling a third, LCP more than doubling, a render-blocking script appearing), not drift. perf 0.85 against a measured floor of 0.96 is 11 points of slack because performance is the noisiest score on a shared runner — the same commit scored 99 and 96 in consecutive runs. Tightening these needs more samples across more runners, not a decision to be stricter today. Note also that `lighthouse` is not a required check (branch protection names only 'Continuous Integration'), so a red here is a visible signal, not a merge block.
